mechanisms.name: strict-validate-path-type on (#11819)
mechanisms.mechanism: Strict validation rejects path characters outside its allowed set unless pathType is ImplementationSpecific. /.well-known contains a '.'; upstream docs describe the allowed set as alphanumerics, '-', '_' and '/', though the source regex may also allow '.'. If '.' is rejected, the admission webhook would refuse the Ingress on its next create or update. If the controller also re-checks existing Ingresses at startup or sync, /.well-known would be dropped or the sync would fail, and the rest of the docs host could be affected; if not, failure would appear only on the next change to the Ingress (e.g. Argo CD selfHeal or resync).
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Not resolved. The / path is fine. The backend itself is fine (nginx pod serves /usr/share/nginx/html/.well-known/security.txt from the wellknown-content ConfigMap). Fallback if rejected: change /.well-known to pathType: ImplementationSpecific (preferred), or set strict-validate-path-type: "false" in controller.config.
citedEvidence: Ingress paths / and /.well-known, both pathType: Prefix
Upstream docs describe the allowed set as alphanumerics, -, _ and /
Neither the changelog nor anything else in upstream/ shows the regex
